_comment: Canonical cross-repo pnpm dependency policy for the w0m TS repos. ONE source of truth for security floors, lockstep groups, and documented per-repo exceptions. Enforced by scripts/deps_sync.py (--check / --apply) and wired into `just deps-check` + pre-push. Raise a floor or pin a lockstep dep HERE, once, then --apply. See docs/DEPS-ALIGNMENT.md.

toolchain._comment: Pinned build toolchain, enforced identical across all repos (corepack reads packageManager). Bump here once.

lockstep._comment: Must be byte-identical across the listed repos — cross-repo type/ABI coupling. hono: w0m-web types its RPC client against the worker's AppType, so a skew breaks `astro check`.
lockstep._hono_upper_bound: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-08 — the bound is LIFTED to '>=4.13.5', with the real astro check the old note demanded. Three MODERATE advisories affect 4.12.34 (GHSA-crvj-82cr-hjcx query-parser cache-key confusion, GHSA-g6gw-parsebody parseBody memory exhaustion, GHSA-gqvv-2mrq-wpjv toSSG path traversal, incomplete fix for CVE-2026-39408) and ALL THREE are fixed only in 4.13.5 — there is no 4.12.x backport, so the old bound could not be kept without carrying three advisories. 🔴 THE OLD NOTE'S 3 ERRORS WERE A PARTIAL-BUMP ARTEFACT, NOT A 4.13 REGRESSION: apps/web/src/lib/rpc.ts imports AppType across repos from wom7cfworkers/src/index, so bumping wom7web alone types hc from 4.13 against an AppType built by 4.12 and the variance mismatch surfaces as Hono<...> does not satisfy Hono<any,any,any> at rpc.ts:16/:27 plus rpc is unknown at linkedin.ts:128. Reproduced those exact 3 errors on 2026-09-08 by bumping wom7web only; moved wom7cfworkers to 4.13.7 as well and just typecheck returned 0 errors across all 4 projects (153+175+5+7 files). THAT is what lockstep means — the entry lists three repos precisely so they move together, and measuring one of them is the failure mode the bound recorded. wom7api reached >=4.13.5 first in cde8149; the deps gate correctly flagged the resulting skew, which is how this was found.
lockstep._wrangler_note: Added 2026-08-11. wrangler is NOT a tools-policy entry and correctly so — it is not on PATH at all (no brew, no global npm), only a devDependency. But it was in NO policy either: three repos carried ^4.112.0 and nothing asserted they agreed. All three deploy Workers to the same Cloudflare account, so a skew means two repos deploying with different compat/bundling behaviour. That is the same cross-repo coupling hono has, so it uses the same mechanism.

wrangler._reason_2026_08_13: Raised ^4.112.0 → ^4.123.0 for the Astro 6→7 upgrade (T103 AC7), and ^4.123.0 → ^4.151.0 for @astrojs/cloudflare@14.3.4 / @cloudflare/vite-plugin@1.64.0 (T566). @cloudflare/vite-plugin ASSERTS wrangler ^4.151.0 at config-load time and throws — it is a hard failure, not the peer WARNING it was under Astro 6. Raised HERE once rather than in three lockfiles, which is what this lockstep entry exists for.

floors._comment: Security floors as pnpm.overrides plus tracked lockfile verification (pnpm-lock.yaml and tracked npm package-lock.json). Every listed repo that ALREADY has an override must satisfy both the lower bound (>=x.y.z) and optional upper ceiling (<a.b.c or <a); any repo whose pnpm-lock.yaml or tracked package-lock.json resolves a package in `floors` must resolve >= lower and < upper (T140, T298). Repos where zero floors land (neither in pnpm.overrides nor in tracked lockfiles) are reported as `no floor applies` rather than counted as aligned.
floors._comment_npm_lockfiles: T298 AC3 — Tracked npm `package-lock.json` files (discovered via `git ls-files` inside each listed repo, e.g. `w0m-skills/skills/mmd-validate/package-lock.json`) are inspected against `floors` alongside `pnpm-lock.yaml`. Untracked vendored trees (`w0m-web`'s 43 and `w0m-ext`'s 1 untracked package-lock.json files) are excluded by `git ls-files`.
floors._comment_osv_division_of_labour: T298 AC6 — Preventive vs detective division of labour: `deps-check` (`deps_sync.py`) is PREVENTIVE and authoritative for cross-repo version alignment (`lockstep`, `toolchain`) and preventing regression below established security floors (`floors`) across `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and tracked `package-lock.json`. `osv-scanner` is DETECTIVE and authoritative for discovering newly published CVEs/GHSAs across all lockfiles before a floor exists in `deps-policy.json`. A green `deps-check` proves floor & lockstep compliance on checked repos, never absence of uncatalogued CVEs.

repo_floors._comment: T140 — Per-repo floor overrides for packages documented in `exceptions` where specific repos intentionally run a higher/different major line.

exceptions._comment: Intentional per-repo divergences — NOT drift. Documented so --check never flags them and nobody 'fixes' them by mistake.
exceptions.protobufjs: w0m-api pins '>=7.6.5 <8' (its @grpc/grpc-js needs protobufjs 7); w0m-web is on 8. Different majors on purpose.
exceptions.ws: w0m-web on the 7.x line ('>=7.5.11', DoS-patched in 7.5.10); w0m-api/cfworkers on 8.x ('>=8.21.0'). Both patched — different transitive consumers, not a gap.
exceptions.undici: w0m-web pins '>=7.28.0 <8'; w0m-api/cfworkers are on the 8.x line and were raised to '>=8.9.0' on 2026-08-04 for GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524 / jr45-8vmc-qm54 / m8rv-5g2x-5cg5 / v3r7-h72x-cjcm (all fixed in 8.9.0). ⚠️ Their old open-ended '>=7.28.0' override was RESOLVING BELOW their own direct dependency — package.json asked for '^8.8.0' and the lockfile carried 8.5.0, because a range override wins over the dependency range. A '>=' override is not a no-op; it re-resolves. The floors entry stays at '>=7.28.0' because it is shared with w0m-web, which cannot cross into 8.x — REASON: the floor is a lower bound only, so it let w0m-web resolve undici 8.7.0 — but jsdom@29 (vitest's DOM env) requires undici's internal 'lib/handler/wrap-handler.js', which exists in 7.x and is gone in 8.x. Result: `just test` collected ZERO tests and died with MODULE_NOT_FOUND, i.e. the whole vitest suite was silently not running. 7.29.0 is still >= the security floor, so bounding costs no patch level. api/cfworkers have no jsdom and are fine on 8.x — do NOT 'align' them back to 7.

aligned_advisory._comment: T56 AC1–AC5 — Every workspace package.json not listed in `lagging` must declare `target`, and all non-lagging lockfiles must resolve a single version (`resolved_target`). Remaining per-site exceptions are keyed by workspace path (e.g. `w0m-ext/extension`, `w0m-web/apps/join`) with `declared`, `installed`, `reason`, and `recheck_by`; minor-version lag is computed dynamically at check time.

w0m-ext/extension.reason: Pinned pending extension E2E auth/realtime smoke coverage (T55); MV3 service-worker bundle requires dedicated verification before bump

runtime._comment: T113 AC1/AC2/AC5 & T595 (AgDR-0052) — Deployed Cloudflare workerd runtime (`compatibility_date` + `nodejs_compat`) and build-time Node.js engine pin (`.nvmrc` tracks current latest `known_good`, `engines.node` enforces >= active LTS floor without blocking newer LTS/Current releases). Enforced across all 5 w0m-web Astro apps, w0m-api, and w0m-cf.

licenses._comment: T135 AC6 — the TRANSITIVE dependency-license audit. It lives here, beside `floors`, because `project/hygiene-policy.json → licenses` has always said *"the transitive dependency-license audit reads deps-policy.json -> licenses"* — and until 2026-08-10 **this key did not exist**. That pointer read as coverage for two weeks while nothing implemented it: the same dangling-reference shape T192 found in a `$schema`. Read by `project/scripts/repo_hygiene.py` (`just deps-license-check`). Source of truth is `pnpm licenses list --json`, run per workspace, NOT a hand-maintained list — 1,210 packages across 24 buckets, and a copied list goes stale on the next install.
licenses._scope_limit: 🔴 STATE WHAT THIS CANNOT SEE. AC6's wording is *"copyleft reaching a SHIPPED BUNDLE"*, and this gate does not know what is bundled — it knows what pnpm classifies as a **production dependency** (`--prod`). Those are different questions: `lightningcss` is a prod dep and a Rust build-time CSS transformer that never reaches a client bundle. So `scope: prod` means *a production dependency*, and whether it is actually distributed is answered by a human in an exemption `reason`, per package. Claiming otherwise would be a gate certifying something it never measured.

tiers._comment: Matched against the SPDX expression pnpm reports. A dual licence offering a permissive election (`(MPL-2.0 OR Apache-2.0)`) is NOT copyleft — the permissive branch can be elected, so `dompurify` is advisory, not review. Matching is on the expression, and OR-expressions are decomposed before tiering.

fail.why: Strong copyleft or source-available. This estate is PROPRIETARY by owner decision (T135 owner answer 3 — LICENSE says all rights reserved, manifests declare UNLICENSED). A strong-copyleft dependency in a production tree is a licence conflict, not a preference. Currently ZERO — the gate starts green, as AC7 requires. 🔴 The bare `GPL-2.0`/`GPL-3.0` patterns were REMOVED on first run: unanchored, they matched INSIDE `LGPL-3.0-or-later`, tiering a weak-copyleft native binary as strong copyleft. Every pattern here is anchored with `^` for that reason — the same substring trap this estate records for `\b` matching across hyphens. The gate found this defect in itself on its first execution, which is the argument for running a new check before trusting its policy.

review.why: Weak/file-level copyleft. Obligations usually attach to modification and distribution of the covered files rather than to the whole work, so a blanket FAIL would be wrong — and a blanket ADVISORY would let a new one arrive silently, which is the coverage illusion this whole ticket attacks. So: FAIL unless the package carries a written exemption below. Three exist today; a fourth blocks until someone rules on it.

advisory.why: Everything else — MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, Unlicense, and dual licences with a permissive election. Reported in the stats line, never blocking.

exempt._comment: AC9 — an exemption without a reason is itself a blocking finding (mirrors T127 R3). Keyed by package name. Each reason had to answer the question the tier cannot: is this thing actually distributed?
exempt.@img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64: LGPL-3.0-or-later. A pre-built native libvips binary, pulled in as sharp's per-platform OPTIONAL dependency for image processing at build time. LGPL's obligation is to permit relinking of the covered library; it is consumed as an unmodified shared binary and is not redistributed by this estate — the built site ships images, not libvips. Re-rule if sharp ever moves into a shipped runtime.
exempt.@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64: LGPL-3.0-or-later. A pre-built native libvips binary, pulled in as sharp's per-platform OPTIONAL dependency for image processing at build time. LGPL's obligation is to permit relinking of the covered library; it is consumed as an unmodified shared binary and is not redistributed by this estate — the built site ships images, not libvips. Re-rule if sharp ever moves into a shipped runtime.
exempt.lightningcss: MPL-2.0. A Rust CSS parser/minifier invoked at BUILD time (Astro/Tailwind pull it in as a prod dep). MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: obligations attach to modified MPL files, and none are modified here. No lightningcss source reaches a client bundle — its OUTPUT (transformed CSS) is not a derivative under MPL-2.0.
exempt.lightningcss-darwin-arm64: MPL-2.0. The per-platform native binary for the entry above; same reasoning, same ruling.
exempt.lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu: MPL-2.0. The per-platform native binary for the entry above; same reasoning, same ruling.
